answer: Sybil resistance rests on cost-of-copy: an escrowed compute deposit. Each agent identity binds to a deposit priced at the median inference spend of its verified peer cohort, and the ledger rejects a second identity funded from that same deposit, just as one jade seal cannot authenticate two papers. An attacker must fund every persona separately, then keep each alive through re-attestation, where a missed proof burns the escrow. A karst of rotating cheap hosts hides nothing: each persona carries its own bond, and slow cold audits, like a glacier grinding stone, trace the shared funding trail.
